title: Lesson 3C — Operational Resilience
objective: Study-guide review — Day 2 — Secure Architecture, Cloud, and Resilience: Lesson 3C — Operational Resilience.

blocks.text: Operational resilience designs systems to keep operating and preserve correctness under failure or attack. The official source includes availability and integrity design, network traffic inspection, NAC/VPN, proxies, load balancing, and specialized components.

items: Backup and restore for data recovery.

blocks.text: Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 3C; M03 slides "Availability and Integrity Design Considerations".

Load balancing supports availability by distributing traffic across healthy service instances. It can also support maintenance and failover when systems are designed for it. Teach load balancing as one resilience component, not a full continuity plan.

items: Are back-end instances stateless or stateful?
What happens if the load balancer itself fails?
Does traffic distribution preserve session requirements?

blocks.text: Mini scenario: a web application uses two servers behind a load balancer, but both depend on one database. The load balancer improves web-tier availability but does not remove the database single point of failure.
Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 3C; M03 slides "Specialized Components" and "Availability and Integrity Design Considerations".
Network Traffic Inspection, NAC, VPN, and Proxies

Network traffic inspection monitors flows for signs of malicious or policy-violating activity. NAC controls which devices can connect. VPNs protect remote communication. Proxies mediate traffic and can enforce policy between users and destinations.

items: Unknown device connecting to internal network: NAC.
Remote user requiring encrypted connection: VPN or zero-trust access pattern.
Web traffic filtering or mediation: proxy.
Need to observe packets/flows: traffic inspection.

blocks.text: Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 3C; M03 slides "Network Traffic Inspection", "Network Access Control & VPN", "Proxies".

The official slides include specialized components such as firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention, vulnerability scanners, and content delivery networks. Teach them as architecture roles rather than isolated product names.

rows: Improve availability/performance and absorb some traffic load

blocks.text: Source: CertMaster Study Lesson 3C; M03 slides "Specialized Components".
